title: One dark night
hookLine: his poem: a soul slips out of the sleeping house to meet her beloved
carry: my house being now at rest

lines: A DARK NIGHT OF THE SOUL.
NOT A SAD POEM. A LOVE POEM.
cards: Someone's going through a dark night of the soul. People use the phrase for burnout, a breakup, a bad year, a crisis of faith. It's on book covers and in song lyrics.

It goes back to a poem of eight short stanzas by a small, thin friar, written, tradition says, close to the months when he climbed out of a prison window. And here's the surprise: it isn't a sad poem. It's a love poem.

teach.b: First, the story. The poem begins, in John's Spanish: "En una noche oscura," on a dark night. A young woman, burning with love, slips out of her house while everyone sleeps.
The first stanza ends "estando ya mi casa sosegada," my house being now at rest. Nobody sees her. She takes a secret stair, in disguise.
She carries no light except the one burning in her heart, and it guides her more surely than the noonday sun, to where her beloved is waiting. Second, who's who.
For John, the young woman is the soul, and the beloved is God.

teach.h: THE SOUL, GOD, THE SLEEPING HOUSE.
teach.b: The sleeping house is everything in us that usually runs the show: our appetites, our worries, our need to control. When the house finally goes quiet, the soul can slip out to meet God. Third, the turn.
Oh night that guided me, she sings, oh night more lovely than the dawn. The darkness isn't the enemy. Without it, she'd never have slipped out unseen.

teach.h: TWO BOOKS TO EXPLAIN ONE POEM.
teach.b: John knew his poem needed explaining, so he wrote two whole books about it, the Ascent of Mount Carmel and the Dark Night.

In them, the night describes how God leads a soul through times when the old lights go out. Over the next days, i'll walk through those books with you. But start here, with the poem: a night that's also a love story.

how: Catholics read John's poem The Dark Night and his commentaries on it, often with a spiritual director, to understand seasons when prayer and faith feel dark, and Carmelites pray and sing his poems.

o: the night the soul, its house quiet, slips out to meet God
the hours of prayer that friars keep through the night
a season of despair when all hope of God is gone

games.q: what's inside the poem — tap the pairs.

s: John's dark night poem is about despair
it's a love poem: a soul slips out at night to meet her beloved.
John wrote two books to explain the poem
the Ascent of Mount Carmel and the Dark Night.
in the poem, the night is the enemy
the soul sings to the night that guided her, more lovely than the dawn.

games.q: you're the young woman in the poem. everyone in the house is asleep, and your beloved is waiting outside in the dark. you have no lamp. what do you do?
o: wait for morning, when you can see.
slip out anyway, guided by the light in your heart.
wake the house and ask for a lamp.
games.why: she goes out with no light but the one burning in her heart, and it guides her more surely than the noonday sun.

practice: Sit in the dark: turn off the light if you can, or close your eyes and cover them with your hands, and let the house of you go quiet, the lists, the plans, the noise. Don't look for anything; just notice that the dark isn't empty.
If you pray, wait for God there, the way the young woman went out to meet her beloved; if you don't, let the dark be a place to rest.

wordCard.voice: Dark night. From John of the Cross's poem: the night in which the soul, its house at rest, slips out to meet God. Not despair, but a love story. Today's word.

orig.note: Spanish: oh night that guided! the turn in John's poem of the dark night, noche oscura.

carryVoice: Your line: my house being now at rest. In the dark, she found the way out. See you tomorrow.
